name: Brad Hicks

bio.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Hicks lists his occupation as small business owner and his background as former president and CEO of The Chamber of Medford & Jackson County.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Small Business Owner Occupational Background: Former President/CEO The Chamber of Medford & Jackson County

source.publisher: Oregon Voters' Pamphlet 2026 General, Jackson/Josephine edition (Book 3), p. 37

bio.statement: Hicks lists prior governmental experience on the Oregon Transportation Vision Panel, Oregon Revenue Restructuring Task Force, Jackson County Public Safety Coordinating Council and Jackson County Airport Advisory Committee.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Oregon Transportation Vision Panel, Oregon Revenue Restructuring Task Force, Jackson County Public Safety Coordinating Council, Jackson County Airport Advisory Committee

source.publisher: Oregon Voters' Pamphlet 2026 General, Jackson/Josephine edition (Book 3), p. 37

positions.statement: Hicks lists affordability as a priority: lower cost of living, lower taxes, less wasteful spending, support for small businesses and tackling the housing crisis.
positions.excerpt: Affordability - Lower the cost of living, lower taxes, cut wasteful spending, support small businesses, and tackle Oregon's housing crisis.

source.publisher: Oregon Voters' Pamphlet 2026 General, Jackson/Josephine edition (Book 3), p. 37

positions.statement: Hicks says he would invest in wildfire prevention, raise education standards and fully support law enforcement.
positions.excerpt: Invest in real wildfire prevention, raise education standards, and fully support law enforcement.

source.publisher: Oregon Voters' Pamphlet 2026 General, Jackson/Josephine edition (Book 3), p. 37

positions.statement: Hicks says he would put Southern Oregon first rather than politics or special interests.
positions.excerpt: Balance - Put Southern Oregon first, not politics or special interests.

source.publisher: Oregon Voters' Pamphlet 2026 General, Jackson/Josephine edition (Book 3), p. 37

positions.statement: Hicks says he could no longer watch Salem raise taxes and the cost of living.
positions.excerpt: I never planned on running for office, but I could no longer sit back and watch Salem politicians raise our taxes, drive up the cost of living, push businesses out of Oregon, and treat Southern Oregon like an afterthought.

source.publisher: Oregon Voters' Pamphlet 2026 General, Jackson/Josephine edition (Book 3), p. 37
